# s341 — The example role matrix has orchestrator rows and a Codex implementer alternative

`relay-roles init` writes an example matrix whose `recommend` resolves the orchestrator on a fresh project: a Claude Code orchestrator first, a Codex one second, and a Codex implementer alternative after the Claude implementer rows. Every role then has a row, except that the architect row stays size L only, so a smaller slice still leaves the architect unmatched. Default picks for every role stay on Claude Code.

**Findings:** s320 relay 2026-10-16 owner question: the relay-roles init example has no orchestrator row, so recommend leaves the orchestrator unmatched on a fresh project; owner chose Claude and Codex orchestrator rows plus a Codex implementer alternative · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-17** — Spec corrected 2026-10-17 after the relay implementer found the architect row (r7) matches size L only: owner chose to keep r7 L-only. Fresh-example tests now expect unmatched == ["architect"] on an S item and [] on an L item; Files gains the lineup() helper and other tests that pin skeleton ids.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**2026-10-17** — Three example rows added to the relay-roles init matrix: r9 (Codex implementer alternative, after the Claude implementer rows), r10 (Claude Code orchestrator, default) and r11 (Codex orchestrator alternative). r7 stays L-only. On a fresh example, recommend resolves the orchestrator, leaves only the architect unmatched on an S item and resolves every role on an L item. Verified: full suite 2326 OK (1 skipped, the SLICER_LEGACY_TREE migrator test), affected 363 OK, slicer check clean, git diff --check clean.

**Not in this slice:** changing the example's rules (the eight rule texts stay as they are, including "No cross-vendor reviewer unless the owner asks"); Codex reviewer, gate or architect rows; changing any existing matrix (only `init` and `init --force` write the example); launching or verifying Codex sessions (the agents repo owns that); bumping the relay contract marker, since the example's rows are data the Setup reads, not a rule an outer session follows.

## Why

s320 (landed 2026-10-16) added the `orchestrator` role and changed the relay Setup to say `recommend` "resolves every role, the orchestrator included, to one row" (`src/slicer/ai.py:385`). Its spec forbade changing the generic example's vendor policy, so `roles.skeleton()` (`src/slicer/roles.py:407`) still holds eight Claude Code rows and no orchestrator row, and `docs/agents.md:101` says so. On a fresh project `recommend` prints `orchestrator  (no matching row)`. On an S or M item its JSON reports `"unmatched": ["architect", "orchestrator"]`, because the example's only architect row (r7) matches size L; on an L item it reports `["orchestrator"]`. So the owner picks the orchestrator by hand. The owner decided on 2026-10-16 to change the example's vendor policy: add a Claude Code orchestrator and a Codex orchestrator, plus a Codex implementer alternative, as this project's own matrix does (r9, r10, r11).

On 2026-10-17 the owner chose to keep r7 L-only (the architect runs only on L slices), after the s341 relay found that the first spec expected an S item to leave nothing unmatched. The Setup text at `src/slicer/ai.py:385` still overclaims for non-L slices; that is a separate later note, not this slice.

Scores: importance 2 because every fresh project starts with an unmatched orchestrator; urgency 1 because only a new `init` or `init --force` is affected and the owner can add rows by hand; effort 1 and size S because it is three rows in one function plus the docs and tests that pin the example. Tree slicer, pass v1.13 beside the other relay follow-ups. Discovered from s320.
